problem: VLN-CE agents predict low-level actions (FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15°) end-to-end from instructions. This forces joint learning of language grounding and control over long horizons (~55 actions per episode), and VLN-style models degrade badly in this setting. The resulting stop-start trajectories are slow to execute on a real robot. Meanwhile, the sim-to-real work of Anderson et al. found that producing candidate waypoints is a bottleneck, and that cannot be studied in the discrete nav-graph simulator.
motivation: The action space is rarely studied in language-guided navigation, but it drives both learning difficulty and real-robot execution cost (velocity changes, planner calls, state-estimation error, hardware strain). Continuous environments allow an agent to predict arbitrary relative waypoints. That makes it possible to study a spectrum between low-level actions and fully continuous waypoints, and to measure both VLN metrics and estimated robot execution time.
key_idea: A language-conditioned waypoint prediction network, trained with DD-PPO, outputs relative polar waypoints: a coarse panorama heading plus an offset and a distance, each continuous, discrete or fixed. A simple low-level navigator executes each waypoint, and varying the expressivity of this output exposes a trade-off between navigation metrics and execution time.
insight: Expressivity creates a clear trade-off. Heading-only models that step a fixed 0.25 m (HPN) beat distance-predicting WPNs by 2-3 SR and in SPL because they take ~4x more actions (33.41 vs 8.41 per episode) and track shortest paths more closely. However, their estimated LoCoBot execution time is roughly double (Val-Unseen EET 297 s vs 153 s) and their SCT is about half (11 vs 23). Among components, offset parameterization matters most: continuous heading offsets beat discrete/fixed offsets by 3-8% SR (Table 1 rows 1&2 vs 3&4). The discount factor governs step size: γ=1 yields HPN-like 0.25 m steps, while γ≤0.5 yields max-distance steps. A distance-scaled slack reward is needed to stop RL from favoring far, unreachable waypoints. A panoramic-to-forward-camera ablation of the pick-pano HPN improves Val-Unseen to 36/32 SR/SPL with a smaller seen-unseen gap, suggesting overfitting. The same agent with the raw low-level VLN-CE action space failed to converge after 300M steps, which points to the long horizon as the key difficulty for RL.
method: Visual encoding: 12-frame panoramic RGB-D (90° HFOV each); RGB via ImageNet ResNet-18, depth via DD-PPO PointNav-pretrained ResNet-50, plus sin/cos pose features per frame and a mean-pooled previous-step context feature from the frame nearest the last predicted heading.

Instruction & history encoding: GloVe embeddings + BiLSTM over the instruction. A visual-history GRU consumes pooled RGB, the previous-frame context and the previous waypoint action (r, sin/cos θ^D, θ^offset).

Cross-modal attention: history state attends over instruction tokens; the attended instruction does spatial attention on each RGB and depth frame, then attention across panorama frames, feeding a second action GRU (all scaled dot-product attention; based on the VLN-CE CMA model).

Waypoint head: a softmax over 12 frames plus STOP (dot product of the action state with per-frame features) gives the coarse heading. Per-frame heads then give an offset in [-15°,15°] and a distance in [0.25 m, 4.0 m], either as truncated Gaussians (continuous), as softmaxes over discrete bins (offset step 5°; distance 0.25-2.75 m step 0.5 m), or as constants (0°, 0.25 m → HPN).

Navigators: a continuous navigator (turn to heading, then move straight the predicted distance; perfect actuation) used in training. At inference, a greedy discrete navigator can instead use VLN-CE's FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° actions for leaderboard comparison.

RL training: DD-PPO (64 GPUs, ~200M steps, ~5 days) with the clipped PPO loss, value loss and per-component entropy bonuses, plus an L1 zero-trending offset regularizer. Reward = success 2.5 (stop within 3 m) − Δgeodesic distance + slack scaled by predicted distance (−0.05·d/0.25 m); γ=0.99.
Robot-time evaluation: LoCoBot MoveBase motion model fitted empirically (rotation quadratic, translation linear) gives Estimated Execution Time (EET). SCT is adapted using a point-turn RRT* oracle.

setting.action_space: predicted relative polar waypoints (12-way coarse heading + offset ±15° + distance 0.25–4 m, or STOP), executed by a continuous turn-then-straight navigator or a greedy discrete navigator using FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15°
setting.privileged: none at test time (perfect actuation assumed; geodesic distance used only in the training reward)

numbers_note: The paper's OS metric is recorded as OSR. EET (seconds) and SCT are reported only for Val-Unseen. Figures (action-space visualizations, LoCoBot fits, qualitative maps) were stripped from the text. Other ablation rows exist but are omitted: Table 1 rows 1/3/4/6 and Table 2 CN/DN checkpoint variants. A forward-facing-camera HPN ablation is given only in text: Val-Unseen 36/32 SR/SPL, Val-Seen 40/37. Checkpoints were selected by Val-Unseen SPL.
results: On the VLN-CE leaderboard test split, HPN+DN reaches 32 SR / 30 SPL (NE 6.65) and WPN+DN reaches 29 SR / 25 SPL. The prior SOTA, CMA+PM+DA+Aug (28 SR / 25 SPL), trained with DAgger, is beaten by +4 SR (14% relative) and +5 SPL (20% relative), even though the discrete navigator was not seen in training. With the continuous navigator, the best WPN (Val-Unseen 36 SR / 30 SPL) trails the best HPN (38 SR / 36 SPL) on standard metrics. However, it cuts estimated LoCoBot execution time from 297 s to 153 s and doubles SCT (23 vs 11); the abstract cites a 2.2x EET reduction vs low-level turn/forward models.
limitations: Assumes perfect actuation and is evaluated only in simulation. Real-robot benefit is estimated from a profiled LoCoBot motion model (EET/SCT), not from real deployment.

More expressive waypoint models score lower on SR/SPL than constrained fixed-step models, and a large gap to discrete nav-graph VLN remains. RL with the raw low-level action space failed to converge after 300M steps.
Very compute-heavy RL (64 GPUs, ~200M steps). Checkpoints are selected on Val-Unseen SPL, and seed variance of ~1 SPL makes small differences insignificant.
builds_on: VLN-CE Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) model (Krantz et al. 2020)
